notes: Primary source: Green-GO's own official product documentation (manual.greengoconnect.com/en/devices/mcx/), cross-checked against the manufacturer product page (greengocom.com/products/mcx) and the Canford UK retailer spec page. Unit is a 1U, 19" rack station, 110mm deep, with a built-in 2W loudspeaker and 3 TFT touchscreens (not physical connectors, omitted from port list). Two ambiguities from the manufacturer's own text are noted per-port above: (1) the headset jack is physically a 4-pin XLR, which has no exact match in the provided connector-id list — xlr5 was chosen as the closest available id, not xlr4-dc (that id is reserved for DC power, not audio signal); (2) the manual's back-panel section header labels genders opposite to its own prose for the two line I/O XLR3 jacks — resolved using the heading text plus standard pro-audio convention (female=input, male=output). The GPIO connector is a D-Sub9 but carries simple opto-isolated contact closures, not RS232 serial data; rs232 was used only as the closest DB9-shaped id in the list. No bandwidth/version grade is stated for the XLR3 audio jacks (standard balanced analog), so grade was omitted there per instructions; the two EtherCON ports are graded eth-100m since the built-in switch is explicitly 10/100 Mbps. One retailer page (Adorama) describes the mic input as "48V phantom power," but the manufacturer's own manual specifies mic power up to 10V — the manufacturer figure was used.

ports.name: MIC
ports.note: Front-panel Neutrik XLR3-Female gooseneck mic input; optionally supplies up to 10V mic power

ports.name: HEADSET
ports.note: Front-panel Neutrik XLR4-Male headset jack (mic + return audio combined on one 4-pin XLR)

ports.name: Line-Input
ports.note: Rear balanced analog line input for injecting audio into a group; manufacturer manual lists this jack as XLR3-Female in its heading but the prose description swaps the gender (says 'male') — going with the heading and standard pro-audio convention (input=female)

ports.name: Line-Output
ports.note: Rear balanced analog line output for extracting audio from a group; same heading/prose gender discrepancy as Line-Input, resolved the same way (output=male)

ports.name: LAN 1
ports.note: Neutrik EtherCON, part of built-in 2-port 10/100Mbps switch; accepts PoE IEEE 802.3af and is the primary power input

ports.name: LAN 2
ports.note: Neutrik EtherCON, second port of the built-in 10/100Mbps switch; unpowered (no PoE)

ports.name: GPIO
ports.note: D-Sub 9 connector providing 2 opto-isolated inputs and 2 outputs for external control; not actually RS232 serial data — rs232 chosen only because it is the closest DB9-shaped connector in the given list

ports.name: DC IN
ports.note: 12V DC barrel jack; secondary power input, used with optional external Green-GO 12V DC power supply when PoE is not used on LAN 1
